_comment: The pictures that STAY in the DCC notes, and the sentence that needs each one.
tools/slim_dcc_figures.py moves every other screenshot out of `learn` and onto
the Reference tab. A picture earns its place here only because a sentence in its
own section points at it - remove it and the sentence dangles. The value is the
caption to give it, because the extractor's own caption for it was filler
Kept because its paragraph says 'In the diagram of the two processes, B and F can
receive remote invocations while C, D and E cannot'.
Kept because its paragraph says 'The smallest sentence in the figure is the one
that matters: installed on one or more servers in your LAN or in the Cloud'.
Kept because its paragraph says 'the diagram shows stratum 1 at the top with
stratum 2 and stratum 3 layered beneath it' - a structure words carry badly.
Kept because its paragraph says 'What the virtual device does, in the diagram:'
and then lists the three things the picture shows.

keep.ch2/lecturemain-ch-2-communication-in-ds: Each process holds objects: B and F can receive remote invocations, while C, D and E can only be invoked locally.
keep.ch2/rest-soap-webservices-lecture-p08.we: The three-tier running example: the client, the web-service application tier, and behind it the data source and the server software, installed on one or more servers in the LAN or in the cloud.
keep.ch3/ch-3-sync-and-cordn-s20-044.webp: The NTP synchronization subnet: stratum 1 machines are connected directly to an accurate time source, and each stratum below is synchronized from the one above it.
keep.ch6/ch6-virtlzn-cloud-ref-arch-resrcprov: What the virtual device does: it remaps guest and real I/O addresses, multiplexes and drives the physical device, and adds I/O features such as copy-on-write disks.

prose.old: The figures below are the reference note's own, and they are worth reading in this order:
prose.new: Five ideas matter here: a message can be stored and forwarded rather than discarded; the temporal relationship between data items decides how they are interpreted. A token bucket is how a stream is paced. A broker with conversion rules between a source and a destination client is messaging middleware; and the interleaving of two streams — a receiver reading two audio units for every video unit — is why synchronicity has to be specified rather than assumed.
prose._why: The seven figures this sentence introduced have moved to the Reference tab. The reading order it gives is the useful part, so it stays - pointed at where the pictures now are.
prose.note: the pointer line this fix installed was retired by the voice pass (tools/voice_rewrite.py): the pictures are reachable from the Reference tab itself, which links each one back to its section, so the notes do not also narrate a reading order. The guard keeps its original purpose - 'the figures below' must not come back - and the present wording is what the check now looks for.

prose.old: The figures below build the socket material up in order:
prose.new: The client and server threads each hold an endpoint object bound to a local I/O port, and the client's socket also carries the destination address and the port number expected at the server. XTI is the transport interface used as the alternative to sockets on other systems, and the MPI send and receive calls are the message-passing primitives underneath the same idea. The Java TCP classes — Socket and ServerSocket, then a complete server example — are the concrete version of the mechanism.
